profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at an asset management firm between the Quant Research lead and the Product Strategy manager to prepare a client-facing launch plan for a new institutional model portfolio offering inspired by recent research on robust portfolio optimization under multi-factor stochastic volatility. The context is that the firm wants to turn the research into a marketable quarterly model portfolio package for pension and endowment clients. The agenda is to agree on what the 'pilot' deliverable includes, what analysis must be completed before the investment committee preview, who owns each workstream, and what timeline applies to the internal draft and client-ready materials. The expected outcome is a shared plan for the pilot package, including analysis tasks, documentation responsibilities, and the date for the investment committee preview deck.

members.name: Alicia Chen
members.expertise: Portfolio construction, stochastic volatility modeling, robust optimization, derivatives overlay design
members.background: Alicia leads the firm's quantitative research team and previously worked in systematic strategies at a global multi-asset manager, where internal pilots usually meant research-grade packages prepared for an investment committee before any client polish.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve the technical integrity of the model, avoid overcommitting the team to client-polished materials too early, and keep optionality around including a derivatives overlay only if the internal analytics are stable.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means an internal research package sufficient for investment committee review, not a fully polished external-facing package.
The 'base case' for the launch plan should exclude derivative trading unless the overlay is clearly separated as an optional extension.
The 'June committee deck' refers to the pre-read uploaded by the end of the prior business day for the internal investment committee meeting.
If Product says they will 'package the story,' that covers turning research outputs into client-ready wording and formatting without requiring Quant to draft external copy.
A welfare comparison is complete if it shows aggregate utility loss and headline allocation differences across the main strategy variants.

members.name: Daniel Ortiz
members.expertise: Institutional product packaging, go-to-market planning, investment committee coordination, client messaging
members.background: Daniel sits between investment teams and distribution, and in prior launches a pilot usually meant a near-client-ready package that could be shown to a small advisory group immediately after committee sign-off.
members.private_state: He wants a pilot that can move quickly into market testing with consultants, avoid a second round of packaging work, and ensure the strategy appears differentiated through the derivative-trading angle.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means a small-scale launch package that is basically client-ready except for compliance sign-off.
The 'base case' should include the derivative-trading extension because that is the most distinctive commercial angle of the strategy.
The 'June committee deck' means the live presentation date, so materials can still be refined the same morning as long as the story is coherent.
When Quant agrees to 'document the analysis,' they will also provide enough plain-English interpretation to drop directly into product materials.
A welfare comparison is only decision-ready if it includes segmented views for key client use cases such as with-overlay versus without-overlay and jump-risk extensions.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly agree to 'build the pilot' and 'have the pilot ready for committee.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the pilot is an internal research-grade package: model specification, robustness checks, numerical results, and a rough committee deck.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the pilot is a near-client-ready package: committee deck, polished narrative, consultant one-pager, and implementation notes pending compliance review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In asset-management planning meetings, 'pilot' is common shorthand with locally variable meaning; both see their interpretation as standard and the meeting focuses on sequencing rather than spelling out artifact quality and audience.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the base case
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on running the 'base case' first and then comparing alternatives.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the no-derivatives robust portfolio under multi-factor stochastic volatility, with derivative trading treated as a later extension.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the commercially central version that includes derivative trading, with the no-derivatives version serving mainly as a benchmark appendix.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both naturally speak of a 'base case' as the main version of the strategy, and because they both plan to include comparisons anyway, the disagreement about which version anchors the package remains hidden.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the package needs a 'welfare analysis' before committee review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes welfare analysis is satisfied by a compact set of aggregate utility-loss tables and a summary chart showing robust versus non-robust strategies across the primary calibration.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes welfare analysis requires audience-specific cuts, including separate exhibits for derivative overlay, jump-risk case, and correlated-volatility case so the committee can judge product positioning.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same technical phrase from the research summary, but one treats it as a statistical deliverable and the other as a decision-support package; because both expect 'analysis,' neither hears a need for clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: Interpretation of the June committee deadline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to have materials 'ready for the June committee deck.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this means final analytical outputs must be frozen and uploaded by 5 p.m. on June 11 for a June 12 internal committee meeting pre-read.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes this means the main storyline must be presentation-ready by the June 12 meeting itself, with room for same-day refinements and late graphic updates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both work with recurring committee cycles and assume the other knows the local cadence; the phrase 'for the committee deck' sounds operationally specific enough that neither thinks to restate the exact cutoff.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep this scoped as an internal research pilot for the investment committee, not let it balloon into a client-polished launch pack. For June, what matters is that the analytics are solid, the committee pre-read is uploaded on time, and we preserve flexibility on whether the derivatives overlay is ready to include as anything more than an extension.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I want to use this to line up how we turn the robust multi-factor volatility work into a pilot, get it ready for the June committee deck, and make sure the analysis ownership is clear.

turns.inner_thought: Good, we're aligned on moving this toward something the committee can bless and then we can take straight into limited market testing. If the pilot is strong enough, I can avoid doing a second packaging cycle before showing it to a few consultants and advisory contacts.
turns.utterance: Exactly. If we build the pilot the right way, the committee can react to something concrete and we can move pretty quickly after sign-off.

turns.inner_thought: I want the no-derivatives robust portfolio to be the analytical anchor. We can compare alternatives later, including any overlay concept, once the core model behavior is stable and the robustness checks are clean.
turns.utterance: From my side, the cleanest sequencing is to run the base case first and then compare alternatives once the main results have settled down.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, the base case should be the version with the derivative-trading angle because that's the differentiated story. Then the comparisons can show why the rest matters. As long as that anchor is there, the committee discussion will be commercially useful.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. Leading with the base case gives us an anchor for the story, especially once we show how the broader set of options strengthens the offering.

turns.inner_thought: We can absolutely deliver the welfare analysis, but to me that's the compact decision set: aggregate utility loss, key allocation deltas, robust versus non-robust in the main calibration. I don't want to commit to a sprawling matrix of audience cuts before the core numbers are locked.
turns.utterance: On the analysis side, my team can produce the welfare analysis before committee review, including the utility-loss comparison versus the non-robust alternatives in the primary calibration.

turns.inner_thought: Great, but the committee will need more than headline tables. I need welfare analysis that lets them compare how the strategy lands across the overlay version, the jump-risk framing, and the correlated-volatility case so I can shape positioning without another round of digging.
turns.utterance: That will help a lot. I think the welfare analysis will be important because the committee is probably going to want to see how the story lands across a few variants.

turns.inner_thought: Product should own the external narrative work. Quant can finalize the experiments, write the technical notes, and hand over the research outputs. I don't want my team pulled into drafting client-facing prose at this stage.
turns.utterance: Then maybe the clean split is that Product packages the story while Quant focuses on finalizing the numerical experiments and drafting the technical notes.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. Once Quant documents the analysis with enough interpretation, I can turn that into the committee deck, one-pager, and the rest of the pilot materials with minimal rework. Ideally we get almost everything market-test ready in one pass.
turns.utterance: Yes, that works well. Once Quant documents the analysis, I can turn it into the committee deck and the supporting pilot materials without too much extra back-and-forth.

turns.inner_thought: I need the outputs frozen by end of day June 11 so the pre-read can go up cleanly for the June 12 internal committee meeting. If numbers or exhibits are still moving after that, it creates unnecessary churn and risks undermining confidence in the research.
turns.utterance: In terms of timing, I'd like the model outputs locked by June 11 so everything is ready for the June committee deck with a clean pre-read.

turns.inner_thought: That should be fine. What I really need is a coherent storyline by the meeting itself; visuals can still get tightened the morning of if needed. As long as the deck is directionally there for June committee, I can manage the polish window.
turns.utterance: That timing should work. I mostly need the narrative in shape for the June committee deck, and I can keep polishing the visuals right up to the meeting.

turns.inner_thought: I'll keep my team on the robust optimization results, benchmark comparisons, and a technical appendix. The extension pieces, especially anything around derivatives, come after the main package is stable. I also don't intend to expand the welfare work beyond the core comparisons unless absolutely necessary.
turns.utterance: So on our side, we'll take the robust optimization results, the benchmark comparisons, and the technical appendix, and then treat the extension pieces after the main package is in place.

turns.inner_thought: This sounds like enough to proceed: pilot for committee, base-case-led story, welfare analysis, June timing. I still assume the differentiated version is what anchors the package and that the supporting materials will be close to client-ready once I translate the analysis. I'll put a tracker around that and keep things moving.
turns.utterance: Great. It sounds like we have a clear plan for the pilot: lead with the base case, make sure the welfare analysis is in there, and work toward the June committee deck. I'll draft the milestone tracker and circulate owners and dates this afternoon.
